body: Approximate time for the Sensex/Nifty to regain a prior peak (levels and dates partly from memory; treat as indicative): 1992 peak 4,467 - exceeded by Sept 1994 (~2.5 years) but that 1994 high then capped the market for most of a decade; 2000 peak ~6,150 - regained around 2004-05 (~4-5 years); 2008 peak 21,206 - briefly regained Nov 2010 (~34 months), sustainably only late 2013 (~6 years of flat returns from the peak); 2015 peak ~30,000 - regained 2017 (~2 years); 2020 COVID crash - new high Nov 2020 (~8-10 months); Sept 2024 Nifty peak ~26,277 - Nifty touched a record 26,310 intraday on 27 Nov 2025 (~14 months) and was ~25,228 on 18 Nov 2026. Pattern: crashes caused by exogenous shocks with policy support (2020, 2016) recover in under a year; crashes after valuation-plus-credit booms (1992, 2000, 2008) take 4-6+ years for large caps and longer for the boom's leading sectors (capital goods 2007 -> ~2021; K-10 tech names never). Small caps take roughly 1.5-2x as long as large caps (see insight:smallcap-drawdown-durations). Implication: the cause of the fall (shock vs bubble unwind) is the best predictor of recovery time.
title: Indian benchmark recovery times after major peaks
